uncertainties: No actual outsourcing contracts, allocations of authority, oversight records, operational evidence, ownership records, smart-contract assessments, confirmation communications or SFC requests are supplied. No finding of fulfillment or breach can therefore be made.

A defensible assessment must distinguish retained accountability and supporting authority arrangements, supervisory conduct in practice, and operational and ownership-record outcomes. Evidence of one category alone does not establish the other categories. The excerpts do not specify which powers must be retained or a complete sufficiency test.

Paragraph 10 supports both an emphasis on non-transferable accountability and a broader reading requiring substantive discharge of responsibility for soundness and records. It does not resolve whether particular failures establish noncompliance irrespective of care, or whether an applicable conduct standard governs fulfillment. Neither a strict outcome guarantee nor a reasonable-care safe harbour is established.

Section 6.11C expressly supplies a care and supervision standard for outsourced valuation. Its standard cannot automatically be transferred to tokenisation; any application or analogy requires justification.

Paragraph 14 most naturally conditions demonstration alone on request. Footnote 5's unqualified wording creates a rival reading concerning demonstration, while also clarifying the recipient and minimum content. The scope of SFC satisfaction over confirmation and the scope of the high-confidence qualifier remain interpretive questions.

No SFC request does not establish approval, satisfaction, absence of vulnerabilities or compliance. It leaves underlying responsibility and the ordinary reading of the confirmation requirement intact.

The full applicable 26EC22 instrument, paragraphs 10–13, footnote 2 and incorporated Appendix factors are unavailable. The packet does not establish instrument versions, complete definitions or applicability to a particular entity or product.

Paragraphs 15 and 16 specify different request-triggered deliverables: technical or operational third-party assurance and a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application. Neither is stated to substitute for the other or automatically discharge paragraph 14.

The supplied intermediary paragraph 13 belongs to a separately described intermediary context; matching paragraph numbers do not establish that it satisfies footnote 5's incorporation of paragraphs 10–13.

Express conduct standard for outsourced valuation provides a relevant comparison, but no supplied incorporation makes it the paragraph 10 tokenisation standard.
Potentially overlapping intermediary responsibility; applicability requires role and activity facts and is not inferred from paragraph numbering.
